description: Backend owner-only routes and pharmacy filtering enforcement. Creates worker/src/routes-owner.js with endpoints for consolidated dashboard, pharmacy management, staff management, and cross-pharmacy reporting. Updates all existing routes (sales, stock, reports, core) to enforce pharmacy_id filtering: system owners can filter by query param or see all pharmacies, regular staff are hard-scoped to their assigned_pharmacy_id. This implements the complete backend authorization model.
steps: Create worker/src/routes-owner.js: Import Hono, lib.js helpers, and need middleware from routes-core.js. Create const app = new Hono(). Add const OWNER_ONLY = need('owner') middleware. Implement GET /dashboard endpoint: check user.is_system_owner, if false throw 403. Query all pharmacies WHERE owner_user_id = user.id. For each pharmacy, aggregate: sales_today (SUM total from sales WHERE pharmacy_id=X AND status='completed' AND sale_date >= today), inventory_value (SUM batches.qty_units * batches.selling_price / drugs.pack_size WHERE drugs.pharmacy_id=X), low_stock_count (COUNT drugs WHERE pharmacy_id=X AND stock_units <= reorder_level), expiry_alerts (COUNT batches JOIN drugs WHERE drugs.pharmacy_id=X AND batches.expiry_date BETWEEN today AND +90 days). Return {total_pharmacies, total_sales, total_inventory_value, total_customers, pharmacies: [...]}.

In routes-owner.js, implement GET /pharmacies, POST /pharmacies, PUT /pharmacies/:id: GET queries SELECT * FROM pharmacy WHERE owner_user_id = user.id ORDER BY name. POST inserts new pharmacy with owner_user_id = user.id. PUT verifies ownership (WHERE id = ? AND owner_user_id = user.id) before updating. Implement GET /pharmacies/:id/stats: verify ownership, return detailed stats (total sales, inventory value, staff count, customer count, top drugs). Implement GET /staff: SELECT users.*, pharmacy_staff_assignments.pharmacy_id, pharmacy.name FROM users LEFT JOIN pharmacy_staff_assignments ON users.id = user_id LEFT JOIN pharmacy ON pharmacy.id = pharmacy_id WHERE pharmacy.owner_user_id = user.id OR users.id = user.id.

In routes-owner.js, implement POST /staff: create user with assigned_pharmacy_id from request. If b.pharmacy_assignments array provided, insert into pharmacy_staff_assignments for each. Implement PUT /staff/:id: update user details, verify ownership via assigned_pharmacy_id or staff assignments. Implement POST /staff/:id/assign: INSERT INTO pharmacy_staff_assignments (user_id, pharmacy_id, role, can_manage_staff) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?), verify pharmacy ownership. Implement DELETE /staff/:id/unassign: DELETE FROM pharmacy_staff_assignments WHERE user_id = ? AND pharmacy_id = ?, UPDATE users SET assigned_pharmacy_id = NULL WHERE id = ? (if no assignments left).

In routes-owner.js, implement GET /sales/consolidated: aggregate sales across WHERE pharmacy.owner_user_id = user.id, group by date, return time series. Implement GET /inventory/consolidated: aggregate batches/drugs across owned pharmacies, return total units, total value, expiry breakdown. Implement GET /reports/comparison: return side-by-side comparison of pharmacies (name, sales_today, sales_month, inventory_value, staff_count, customer_count, status). Export default app at end.

Update worker/src/index.js: import ownerRoutes from './routes-owner.js'. After existing route registrations (around line 60), add: app.route('/api/owner', ownerRoutes). Ensure this is after auth middleware but before notFound handler.

Update worker/src/routes-sales.js POST /sales (around line 25): Read const pharmacy_id = c.get('pharmacy_id'); const is_system_owner = c.get('is_system_owner'). If NOT is_system_owner, set pharmacy_id on INSERT: INSERT INTO sales (..., pharmacy_id) VALUES (..., ?). If is_system_owner and no pharmacy_id in context (user hasn't selected one), throw bad('Please select a pharmacy before creating a sale'). Update GET /sales (list): add filtering: let wherePharmacy = ''; const args = []; if (is_system_owner) { const filter = int(c.req.query('pharmacy_id')); if (filter) { wherePharmacy = 'AND s.pharmacy_id = ?'; args.push(filter); } } else { wherePharmacy = 'AND s.pharmacy_id = ?'; args.push(pharmacy_id); }. Apply to query: SELECT * FROM sales s WHERE status='completed' ${wherePharmacy}. Update GET /sales/:id: add ownership check WHERE id = ? AND (pharmacy_id = ? OR ? = 1), bind id, pharmacy_id, is_system_owner.

Update worker/src/routes-stock.js GET /drugs (around line 35): add same pharmacy filtering pattern as sales. const is_system_owner = c.get('is_system_owner'); const pharmacy_id = c.get('pharmacy_id'); let wherePharmacy = ''; const args = [today, today, today]; if (is_system_owner) { const filter = int(c.req.query('pharmacy_id')); if (filter) { wherePharmacy = 'AND d.pharmacy_id = ?'; args.push(filter); } } else { wherePharmacy = 'AND d.pharmacy_id = ?'; args.push(pharmacy_id); }. Apply to main query. Update POST /drugs: set pharmacy_id on INSERT. If is_system_owner and no pharmacy_id, require pharmacy_id in body or throw error. Update PUT /drugs/:id: verify ownership via pharmacy_id match. Update GET /batches, POST /batches: filter through drugs table join.

Update worker/src/routes-reports.js GET /dashboard (around line 15): Apply pharmacy filtering to all queries. const is_system_owner = c.get('is_system_owner'); const pharmacy_id = c.get('pharmacy_id'); const own = user.role === 'cashier' ? ' AND s.cashier_id = ' + user.id : ''; const pharmacyFilter = is_system_owner ? (int(c.req.query('pharmacy_id')) ? ' AND s.pharmacy_id = ' + int(c.req.query('pharmacy_id')) : '') : ' AND s.pharmacy_id = ' + pharmacy_id;. Apply to all sales queries: WHERE status='completed'${pharmacyFilter}${own}. Update GET /reports/daily, GET /reports/profit, and all other report endpoints with same pattern.

Update worker/src/routes-core.js GET /users (around line 115): Add pharmacy filtering. If is_system_owner, show users from all owned pharmacies: SELECT u.* FROM users u LEFT JOIN pharmacy p ON u.assigned_pharmacy_id = p.id WHERE p.owner_user_id = ? OR u.id = ?. Else show only users from same pharmacy: WHERE assigned_pharmacy_id = ?. Update GET /expiry-alerts (around line 230): filter via drugs.pharmacy_id. Update GET /stock-alerts: same pattern. Update GET /health-check: filter stats queries by pharmacy_id.

Test owner routes: npm run dev:api, use curl or Postman to test GET /api/owner/dashboard with system owner token (should return data), with regular user token (should return 403). Test GET /api/owner/pharmacies creates and lists. Test POST /api/owner/staff creates user and assigns. Test pharmacy filtering: create drug in pharmacy 1, switch context to pharmacy 2 (via ?pharmacy_id=2), verify drug not visible. Verify non-system-owner users cannot access different pharmacy data even with query param.
acceptance_criteria: worker/src/routes-owner.js exists with all specified endpoints (dashboard, pharmacies CRUD, staff CRUD, sales/inventory/reports consolidated)
Owner routes require system owner role and verify pharmacy ownership
All existing routes (sales, stock, reports, core) enforce pharmacy_id filtering
System owners can optionally filter by ?pharmacy_id= query param or see all owned pharmacies
Regular staff are always hard-filtered to assigned_pharmacy_id regardless of query params
INSERT operations include pharmacy_id (either from context or explicitly required)
Data isolation verified: pharmacy A staff cannot see pharmacy B data
verification: npm run dev:api starts without errors and routes-owner.js is registered
curl http://localhost:8787/api/owner/dashboard with system owner token returns consolidated metrics
curl http://localhost:8787/api/owner/dashboard with non-owner token returns 403 Forbidden
Create two pharmacies via POST /api/owner/pharmacies, verify both appear in GET /api/owner/pharmacies
Create user assigned to pharmacy 2 via POST /api/owner/staff, verify assigned_pharmacy_id = 2
Add drug to pharmacy 1, login as pharmacy 2 user, verify GET /api/drugs does not return the drug
As system owner, GET /api/drugs?pharmacy_id=1 returns pharmacy 1 drugs only
As system owner, GET /api/drugs with no query param returns all drugs from all owned pharmacies
Test that pharmacy_id query param is ignored for non-system-owner users (always use assigned_pharmacy_id)
